correctness.rationale: For centered X the explained variance is exactly sum_y M_y^2/P_y with all P_y>0 for contrast below one. The Walsh expansions follow from the independent common-contrast likelihood; sign reversal gives evenness. To justify the uniform Lipschitz order-six remainder, choose a complex contrast disk where the absolute sum of nonconstant denominator terms is below 1/2 for every threshold vector. Step-function moments are uniformly Lipschitz from their changing intervals; on the disk both the rational expression and its threshold differences are bounded, the latter by C_k times threshold distance. Cauchy coefficient bounds and a geometric tail give the stated Lipschitz estimate on a smaller disk. At fourth order the terms are E[L2^2+2L1 L3-2L1 L2 Q1+L1^2(Q1^2-Q2)] with L_j the numerator and Q_j the denominator Walsh degree j; E[L1 L3]=0. At t_i=1/2+d_i, b_ij=O(||d||^2), a_i=-2d_i and a_ij=1-2|d_i-d_j|, so only -2 sum c_i c_j a_ij generates the linear +sum|d_i-d_j|/4. The order-two loss is -sum d_i^2/2+sum d_i^4. Compact uniform order-two convergence brings every optimizer to the repeated midpoint; the quadratic loss and linear difference bound then force O_k(epsilon^2). Sorting reduces the scaled energy to a square around (2i-k-1)/4, with unique sorted maximizer and gain k(k^2-1)/96. Uniform scaled convergence plus comparison to this feasible trial design proves the claim for all global optimizers. The positive scaled spacing implies their eventual distinctness. Independent polynomial-cell calculations checked exact dyadic coefficients through order six in 28 finite designs, k=2..8, with replication and perturbed offsets; replay /workspace/branches/spectral_design_replays.js, thresholdCheck. Frozen CHECKS.txt reports 40 finite inequalities; verify.py was inspected but not executed. Neither finite check proves uniqueness at finite contrast or a growing-budget limit.

value.rationale: At leading order the globally optimal thresholds are indistinguishable from full replication, so neither first-order weak-channel information nor an exact pair design determines whether spreading helps for arbitrary budgets. The result resolves where every global optimizer goes at the first scale that distinguishes locations, and computes the first positive value advantage with explicit dependence on budget, without imposing symmetry. This is an intrinsic design question, not a routine reparametrization or a numerical gain.
